cannibalisation_check.verdict: No cannibalisation of the target keyword: no page of ours targets 'wedding witnesses', 'how many witnesses' or 'who can be a witness'. Partial, manageable overlap with the pillar on the two-witness rule and NOIM witnesses. Write the spoke and link up.

cross_market_insights: Same SERP in all three cities: a commercial witness-for-hire page (Online Weddings Australia) in the top two, a five-year-old US officiant post (marryus.org, refers to a 'marriage license') at #3, then celebrant blogs, a drive-through wedding business, Instagram posts and local marriage offices selling witnesses at $30 to $130. A state government page is #1 in Brisbane and #2 in Sydney on authority only.

Every Australian snippet gives the same one-line answer (two witnesses, 18 or over). Nobody goes beyond it with official sources: who cannot be a witness, ID, understanding the language, what they sign, or the difference between NOIM witnesses and ceremony witnesses (only a Melbourne marriage office mixes the two).

No page covers witnesses when Australians marry abroad (Italy, Greece, France, Bali), or who witnesses which ceremony when you marry legally at home and celebrate overseas. This is our gap and fits the destination audience.

PAA is thin and drifts off-topic; the only on-topic question is 'Who can you have as witnesses at a wedding?' (all three cities), plus 'What happens to a marriage that is not registered?' (Melbourne, Brisbane). Related searches add 'How many wedding witnesses do you need', 'Is being a witness at a wedding important', 'Wedding witness requirements' and registry or courthouse weddings.

Search intent is mixed: informational (rules) and transactional (hire a witness, for elopements and registry weddings). Our luxury audience will not hire strangers; the luxury angle is choosing the right two people, getting them there, and briefing them.
payload.recommended_angle: Two witnesses is the easy part. Answer 'how many and who' in the first 60 words with the official source, then do what nobody ranking does: separate ceremony witnesses from NOIM witnesses, show the rules in Italy, Greece, France and Bali, explain who witnesses which ceremony when the legal part is at home and the celebration is abroad, and cover the invisible work of getting two adults with the right ID to the right place on time.
